fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the street entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the entry point at night or in low visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive to maintain clearance for fire apparatus and emergency vehicles traveling to the structures.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach both the main residence and the detached structure without obstruction.
• Post a diagram of the property at the driveway entrance showing the location of both structures, the circular driveway, and any dead ends so arriving responders can orient quickly.
• Maintain the circular driveway surface to support the weight of fire apparatus, which typically exceed 50,000 pounds.
• Keep the circular driveway free of landscaping features, decorative objects, or parked vehicles that reduce the turning radius available to large emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can identify it, access it, and work around it without obstruction.
• Mark any gates or walkway access points with reflective hardware so responders can locate secondary paths between structures at night.
• Identify and mark the nearest exterior utility shutoffs on both structures so responders can locate them without searching.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between individual trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the structure so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear brush and ground vegetation from both sides of the driveway along its full length so vehicles can pass safely.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep the full width and height open for emergency vehicles.
• Thin mixed vegetation and shrubs in the brush area closest to the structure to reduce the concentration of burnable material near the building.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation in the open clearing regularly to keep it short and reduce the amount of dry material that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Clear vegetation from the rear of the structure to create better access for firefighters working in that area.
• Remove dead plant material from within shrub and brush areas near the structure.
• Keep the area immediately around any outbuildings or improvements clear of shrubs and ground vegetation.
